subject: chemistry
question_text: Explain the difference between emission and absorption spectra.

verification.note: Chapter 1 is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.48-52), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 2+2 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. The book prints this answer as a three-row comparison table; a table is fully accepted in the examination and is the faster way to write it. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25 (audit round): the insider note said three rows while the emission step carries three points and the absorption step four, because bright against dark is a numbered point on one side and the boxed lead line on the other; the note now names the three rows, says which line carries the third on the absorption side, and calls the matching-lines point an extra. No marked line changed.

steps.label: Emission spectrum
lines: 1. Formed when an electron jumps from a
higher orbit to a lower orbit.
3. It shows bright lines on a dark background.
steps.why: An electron falling to a lower orbit releases the energy difference as a photon of one fixed frequency, so the spectrum records what the atom gave out. That is why the lines are bright.
common_mistakes: Writing higher to lower for both spectra. The direction of the jump is the whole difference.
Giving only one point. Three numbered points are expected for two marks.
steps.memory_tip: Emission means giving out. The electron falls and the lines are bright.
steps.margin_note: Number the points. A three-point list reads as three separate ideas.

steps.label: Absorption spectrum

lines.text: Absorption: dark lines on a bright background

lines: 1. Formed when an electron jumps from a
lower orbit to a higher orbit.
3. The dark lines fall exactly where the
emission lines of the same atom appear.
steps.why: The atom takes out of the incoming white light exactly the frequencies it would otherwise emit, so those frequencies are missing and appear as dark lines. This matching of positions is what identifies the element.
common_mistakes: Writing bright lines for the absorption spectrum.
Saying the energy is absorbed continuously. It is absorbed in quanta, in fixed amounts.
steps.memory_tip: Absorption means taking in. The electron rises and the lines are dark.
steps.margin_note: The third point, that the lines match, is the one most students leave out.

insider_note: Write it as a two-column table with three rows: the direction of the jump, the energy in quanta, and bright lines on dark against dark lines on bright, which the boxed line carries on the absorption side. Missing the direction loses both halves at once. The extra point that the dark lines sit exactly where the emission lines are is worth writing when there is room.
